newsitem.title: YEMEN: French hostage in Yemen handed over to mediators.
newsitem.headline: French hostage in Yemen handed over to mediators.

text.p: A French diplomat, kidnapped in Yemen five days ago, was handed over to mediators by his captors on Saturday who were expected to hand him over to the authorities shortly, a Yemeni official said.
"The French diplomat will be handed over to Yemeni authorities and the French Embassy within three hours," the spokesman for the governer of Marib province Abdul Wali al-Shumairi told Reuters.
He said the captors, members of al-Toaiman tribe, released their hostage to three prominant tribal chiefs who were mediating on behalf of the government.
"Three prominant tribal chiefs negotiated with al-Toaiman tribe to secure the release," he said.
The diplomat, seized on Monday as he drove his car in Sanaa, has not been identified. He was being held in Marib province, 170 km (100 miles) north of the Yemeni capital.
French embassy officials have refused to give details on the diplomat, who Yemeni authorities say is a first secretary at the embassy.
The kidnappers had dropped their demands earlier and asked for a guarantee that they would not be prosecuted if they release their hostage.
It was not immediatly clear what arrangements were reached by the negotiators.

The Toaiman tribe demanded government compensation for losses inflicted on homes, farms, water pumps and wells by floods that killed 65 people in June. It also wants more job opportunities and the settlement of a land dispute.
Yemen on Thursday said mediators were making progress with the captors but had asked for more time.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners for use as bargaining chips.
At least two diplomats, an American and a Saudi ambassador, have been among the kidnap victims.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
